title: Additive subset-SUM spectrum (F15, open) vs multiplicative subset-PRODUCT spectrum (proven <=n): SAME mu_n, opposite collapse - the dilation orbit bridges them
evidence: Two NEW exact probes at PROPER dyadic subgroup primes (n=8/16/32/64/128, beta=4 and beta=5, q~n^beta, n<<sqrt q, q==1 mod n): scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C074_dilation_orbit.py and probe_C074_growth_law.py. THREE pieces. (1) PRODUCT spectrum == exactly n: reconfirmed in every case (#PROD==n True for all n,t,beta), matching the already-axiom-clean Lean theorem ProximityGap.SubsetProductSpectrum.subsetProduct_spectrum_card_le_subgroup + ..._subgroup_ceiling_sharp (Frontier/SubsetProductSpectrum{,Subgroup}.lean: prod_{x in S} x = g^{Sum exponents} lands in mu_n, exactly n exponent residues). (2) DILATION-ORBIT BRIDGE = PROVEN exact law. g*(sum_{x in S} x) = sum_{x in g*S} x and g*S is again a t-subset of mu_n, so the sum spectrum Sigma_t is invariant under x->g*x, hence a union of mu_n-orbits + possibly {0}. The action is FREE on nonzero sums: for s!=0, g^j*s=s forces g^j=1 i.e. j==0 (g has order n), so EVERY nonzero orbit has size EXACTLY n. Probe column allsize=n? is True in 100% of cases (n up to 128, t up to 6); equivalently #(Sigma_t\{0}) ≡ 0 (mod n) in every row (nz%n==0 uniformly). This is a rigorous identity, not a probe coincidence - it is the bad-scalar coset-quantization (matches lacBad_smul_closed), confirming the prize-relevant bad-scalar count is always a multiple of n (a union of full mu_n orbits, >=n if any nonzero bad scalar). (3) The COLLAPSE question is the OPPOSITE of the product side. K = #Sigma_t/n = #orbits grows combinatorially: ratio #orbits/[C(n,t)/n] = 0.38..0.99 and trends to 1 as q grows (n=128,t=2 -> 0.992), so #Sigma_t ~ C(n,t) = super-polynomial in n at growing t - the full subset-SUM set is near-MAXIMAL, NOT collapsed to poly*n like the product set. So C074's framing 'same domain, two subset-operations, provably-opposite spectrum sizes (n vs near-C(n,t))' is CONFIRMED exactly.
honest_note: PROVEN here: (a) product spectrum == n (Lean axiom-clean already in tree), (b) the dilation-orbit freeness identity #nonzero-orbit = n hence #bad ≡ 0 mod n (a clean exact algebraic fact for all q,n - candidate for a short Lean lemma g*subset-sum=subset-sum-of-g*S + order-n freeness), (c) the sum spectrum is near-maximal C(n,t), the opposite extreme of the product collapse. NOT closed: the actual prize core. The dilation law bounds the bad set BELOW (>=n) and quantizes it (union of mu_n cosets), but the prize needs an UPPER bound #bad = O(n) = O(1) orbits at the WINDOW-INTERIOR radius. The number of orbits K at the prize radius IS the open quantity, and it equals subset-sum equidistribution of the class set in mu_n = exactly the BGK / generalized-Paley sup-norm wall (same conclusion C044 reached independently from the e_1-of-class-SUM identity). The full subset-sum set (this probe) is the wrong object for the bound (it is near-maximal); only the window-restricted bad set could be O(n), and that is unproven. Probes are exact integer/mod-q but small (n<=128); the freeness identity is a closed-form fact valid for all q,n (g has order n) so it is rigorous beyond the sampled range. No closure - honest. The PARTIAL is: orbit law + product/sum opposition proven; delta* collapse welds to BGK.
reduced_to: Whether the WINDOW-INTERIOR ladder bad-scalar count stays O(n) (= O(1) mu_n-orbits), equivalently whether the number of distinct (k+1)-subset sums of mu_n that arise as bad ladder ratios at radius in (1-sqrt rho, 1-rho-Theta(1/log n)) is O(1) orbits. The dilation law makes this exactly 'count mu_n-orbits of window-bad subset sums'; the full (unrestricted) subset-sum set is near-maximal C(n,t) so the restriction to the window is essential and unproven.
wall: BGK / generalized-Paley sup-norm (subset-sum / Gauss-period equidistribution of the class set in mu_n): the orbit count K = #bad/n is governed by incomplete character-sum cancellation over the thin subgroup mu_n, the 25-year-open core; the dilation orbit gives the >=n floor and mod-n quantization but no matching O(n) ceiling.
